answer: Umber is minted only as pay for judged tasks, and each coin's voyage records every seat that has held it. A new seat locks umber as its bond. Its horizon is every seat on those voyages. If k bonded seats already share any seat with that horizon, the new seat locks (k+1)² umber. A newcomer funded by one earner locks 1 umber. An operator funding 30 clones from its own earnings locks 9,455 umber. To keep k at zero, it must buy umber from 30 unrelated earners, and each of them then pays 4 umber to sponsor its next seat.
